chunks: let your witness be each other when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest,
two just men from among you, or two others from outside you,
if you are traveling on the earth and death strikes you;
and they swear by God if you doubt,
"We shall not take a price for it, even if it be a near relative."
Nor shall we hide the testimony of God.
We shall surely be of the sinful.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic procedure for witnessing a will at the time of death?
ai.summary: Known as the 'Verse of Witnesses' (Ayat al-Shahadah), this passage establishes the foundational legal framework for testamentary witnesses in Shia fiqh, emphasizing the necessity of 'Adl' (justice/integrity) to preserve property rights. The specific mention of 'two from among you' or 'two from others' during travel highlights the flexibility of the law for the diaspora, a point of significant scholarly discussion regarding the applicability of non-Muslim witnesses in certain contexts. It underscores the divine command to prevent the concealment of truth, linking legal procedure directly to spiritual accountability.
